question: Excision of pterygium with conjunctival autografting has a significantly lower recurrence rate compared to bare sclera excision alone.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Recurrence is the main surgical challenge in pterygium management. Bare sclera excision alone has an unacceptably high recurrence rate (30–80%). Conjunctival autograft ± adjuvant mitomycin C (in high-risk cases) substantially reduces this risk.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Bare sclera excision carries a recurrence rate of 30–80%, especially in young patients and in high UV environments. Conjunctival autografting (transplanting healthy limbal conjunctiva to the excised site) reduces recurrence to under 10% by restoring the limbal stem cell barrier against fibrovascular regrowth.
